facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest support is the June 2026 refinancing, which extended the term loan to 2033 and the revolver to 2031 and leaves no large maturity before 2031, together with steady cash interest cover and a seasonal pattern in which the December quarter carries the highest earnings: adjusted EBITDA in the December 2025 quarter was 1.41x the September 2025 quarter. A completed sale-leaseback of the Saxoprint facility, now held for sale, would cut net debt, and net leverage returning towards the 3.38x seen at June 2026 would reverse the concern. Further revolver drawings above USD 50.0 million, or a fall in trailing EBITDA, would strengthen it. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against concern is restraint. Cimpress has never paid a dividend and does not expect to, repurchases fell from 44.76% to 17.65% of operating cash flow between FY2024 and FY2026 and have not been made since February 2026, the credit agreement restricts both dividends and purchases of ordinary shares, and the auditor and management report clean controls. A completed sale-leaseback of the Saxoprint facility, valued at 32.92% of the purchase consideration, would offset part of the acquisition cash. The view would improve if the executed documents showed tight limits on restricted payments, if the Board paired its repurchase authorisation with a debt reduction target, or if the sale-leaseback closed. It would worsen if repurchases resumed while the revolver stayed drawn, if the proxy statement showed one holder with control or board nominee rights, if the documents allowed wide capacity for shareholder payments, or if minority put payments exceeded their carrying value. facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Net debt stood at 3.93x trailing reported EBITDA at 30 September 2026, or 3.96x pro forma for a minority put payment due in the December 2026 quarter, against 3.38x at 30 June 2026, which precedes the July 2026 Saxoprint purchase and has no pro forma figure established. The main downside path runs through VistaPrint, which earns 61.14% of segment EBITDA. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - The refinancing runway is the main support, and the credit case rests on refinancing the 2032 notes before mid-2032. The notes and the term loan are 97.11% of principal; the term loan is due in June 2033 but moves to 16 June 2032 if the notes are not repaid, refinanced or extended, and the revolver matures in 2031 with 14.0% drawn. Nothing material falls due before 2031 apart from scheduled amortisation and small other debt, so near-term repayment is not the pressure point. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; calculation D19; calculation D11

facts.text: - Leverage has stepped up and the cushion is thinner. Net debt rose 11.80% in the September 2026 quarter because Saxoprint was paid for from cash and the revolver while trailing EBITDA slipped, taking net leverage on reported EBITDA from 3.38x at June to 3.93x, or 3.96x pro forma for the minority put payment due in the December 2026 quarter. On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the ratio is 3.39x, and 3.50x without the tariff refunds that sit in the adjusted figure. No pro forma for the July 2026 purchase is established against the June figure. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D01; calculation D02; calculation D03; calculation D04; calculation D05; calculation D06; calculation D07

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a weakening view is the structure of the debt and the seasonal rebuild. No large maturity falls due before 2031, interest cover has held between 3.34x and 3.67x, and cash rose 28.69% between September and December 2025 as the December quarter delivered adjusted EBITDA of 1.41x the September quarter, so the September 2026 trough may reverse. Management also has levers: repurchases have been paused since February 2026, capital spending is 4.48% of revenue, and a completed sale-leaseback of the Saxoprint facility, valued at 32.92% of the purchase consideration, would cut net debt. The view would improve if net leverage returned towards 3.38x after the December 2026 quarter and cash conversion stopped falling. It would worsen if drawings passed USD 50.0 million, if trailing EBITDA kept falling, or if repurchases resumed while the revolver stayed drawn. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D02; calculation D11; calculation D13; calculation D17; calculation D25

facts.text: Margins can be defended only partly. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense in a fragmented market, which limits pricing, while scale and central purchasing give Cimpress a cost edge over smaller printers. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale and market position is strong on evidence: the group says it is the largest in its space, with USD 3.7 billion of revenue and VistaPrint at a 20.29% segment margin. Competitive advantage is average, resting on scale purchasing and the platform but with price-sensitive buyers. Business diversification is average, because VistaPrint produces 61.14% of segment EBITDA even though five segments and two continents are present. Cost and capex flexibility is average, margin stability is weak, and free cash flow stability is weak, given conversion of 26.70% and a margin down 2.43 percentage points since FY2024. The ability to refinance is average, on a long runway but no market evidence. Liquidity is weak at the seasonal low, at 0.19x of debt, and financial policy and governance is average, with transparent reporting but a value-per-share objective that competes with debt reduction. The trend is weakening. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D10; calculation D12; calculation D15; calculation D21; calculation D26

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 months to 24 months the December 2026 quarter decides whether cash and leverage recover: it carries the peak earnings, and the Saxoprint integration, the planned sale-leaseback and a further claim of about USD 10 million for tariff refunds are tailwinds, against headwinds from start-up costs for the North American network, tariffs, energy and a minority put payment. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The most credible downside begins with weaker small-business demand or higher cross-border tariffs while North American start-up costs persist. VistaPrint, which earns 61.14% of segment EBITDA, loses volume and margin first; group EBITDA falls, and adjusted free cash flow, already 26.70% of adjusted EBITDA, turns negative after capital spending. A 10% fall in trailing reported EBITDA, with net debt unchanged, would lift net leverage to 4.37x, or 4.40x pro forma for the minority put payment due in the December 2026 quarter. Cash and USD 197.7 million of undrawn capacity cover the seasonal trough, but drawings above USD 50.0 million bring the leverage test into play, and the next levers are to stop repurchases, slow capital spending and complete the sale-leaseback. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through the December quarter, but the margin for a second weak year is thin. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation D11; calculation D12; calculation D21; calculation D26

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Cimpress presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, a prepaid VistaPrint franchise and a runway to 2032, but credit quality is constrained by rising leverage, falling cash conversion and margin compression. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but weakening because capital spending and cost of revenue are rising faster than earnings. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA recovering before the notes approach their June 2032 window, and on the financial policy staying restrained. The primary downside path is a VistaPrint earnings shortfall that turns free cash flow negative while leverage is already high. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, ratings and market evidence, and management guidance. Top risk: VistaPrint earnings concentration combined with thin liquidity at the seasonal low. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D03; calculation D12; calculation D21

## Findings
### Bottom line

The four periodic filings are enough to support a credit snapshot of CIMPRESS plc, but the three earnings releases are empty and no loan or bond documents were supplied, so creditor protections can be read only as the company summarises them.

The annual report for the year to June 30, 2026 and the quarterly reports for December 2025, March 2026 and September 2026 carry full statements, the debt note, liquidity and covenant wording, and the latest was signed seven days before the as-of date. The earnings releases are wrappers around slide images that were not supplied, so the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 has no release of its own and must be derived from the full year less nine months. Covenant headroom, guarantor and security detail cannot be tested without the loan and bond documents, and ratings, market prices and company guidance are absent.

spans.text: # CIMPRESS plc financial foundation
## Request

Financial foundation for CIMPRESS plc (issuer id cmpr), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the consolidated group's statements, debt, liquidity and leverage from the 2026 annual report and the three quarterly reports, in US dollars.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-08-07 | 151f9f0c267c42ae21f0ccdb2698ae7b00f08c12c11ea93c9eead2d225985251 | Audited statements for FY2024 to FY2026, debt note, liquidity, non-GAAP reconciliations, segments and subsequent events. |

| 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmpr-20251231.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-01-29 | 5912ac914c426cabed13522689ed2e56011a6c1882bd27d73724a7b41632fcbe | Second quarter and six-month FY2026 statements, balance sheet at 2025-12-31 and debt terms before the June 2026 amendment. |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_cmpr-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-04-30 | f9c2a0f9fab56a82d76e0a19184ee2eca64fd97201bf2165c7319cc1b208da3c | Third quarter and nine-month FY2026 statements, balance sheet at 2026-03-31 and the nine-month figures that give the fourth quarter. |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-10-29 | a95f01276eb1e8e5ae3ae14e80d4bc7b302a4218d45429f246acfed151ff64a5 | First quarter of FY2027 statements, latest debt, liquidity, Saxoprint acquisition and segments. |
| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | CP-0 | 028e31a3e82855aedf0db796217ece1d76cd2cfc2b74079745bbc8f5df1ad463 | Confirms the four filings are usable, the three earnings release files hold no text, and no legal documents, ratings or market data were supplied. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage rose and liquidity fell in the September 2026 quarter, with net debt at 3.93x trailing reported EBITDA, because the Saxoprint acquisition was funded from cash and the revolver while trailing earnings slipped, so creditors hold a thinner cushion going into the seasonal peak.

Net debt rose 11.80% in the quarter, and undrawn revolver capacity fell from USD 232.7 million to USD 197.7 million as USD 35.0 million was drawn. On the issuer's own adjusted EBITDA net leverage is 3.39x and cash interest cover 4.11x, but that measure keeps USD 14.4 million of one-off tariff refunds.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 20–21, 33, 46; calculation C35; calculation C41
### Key findings

- Leverage improved through FY2026 and gave much of it back in the September 2026 quarter. Net debt to reported EBITDA was 3.68x at June 2025, 3.38x at June 2026 and 3.93x on a trailing basis at 30 September 2026, and on adjusted EBITDA it was 3.12x, 2.97x and 3.39x. Reported EBITDA rose in FY2026 while net debt barely moved, but the Saxoprint purchase and a seasonal inventory build then cut cash while trailing EBITDA slipped, so creditors enter the December peak with less margin.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 87, 117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 18, 43–44; calculation C01; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C15; calculation C16

- Cash interest cover is steady rather than improving. EBITDA over cash interest paid was 3.34x, 3.67x and 3.54x at the same dates, and 4.11x on adjusted EBITDA at 30 September 2026. Cash interest paid has been flat to slightly lower, so cover moves with earnings, and 67.73% of principal floats on Term SOFR: a 100 bp rise in rates would add USD 7.4 million to annual interest after swaps.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 21, 50; calculation C17; calculation C36; calculation C43

- Cash conversion is weakening as capital spending rises. Adjusted free cash flow was 55.70% of adjusted EBITDA in FY2024, 34.17% in FY2025 and 26.70% in FY2026, while capex including capitalised software rose from 3.44% of revenue to 4.48%, mostly for manufacturing and automation equipment in the North American network. The latest quarter was an adjusted free cash outflow of USD 9.25 million, so less internally generated cash is available for debt reduction while acquisitions and share purchases compete for the same cash.

- Liquidity thinned in the quarter. Cash plus undrawn revolver capacity was 0.19x of total debt at 30 September 2026 against 0.30x at 30 June 2026. The leverage covenant applies only if drawings exceed 20% of the USD 250.0 million commitment, which is USD 50.0 million, and drawings were USD 35.0 million, so USD 15.0 million of further drawings would bring the test into play; the lender-defined ratio against its 4.50x limit is not printed, so headroom is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 72, 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 46; calculation C37; calculation C38; calculation C39

- Maturities are distant but concentrated. The USD 525.0 million of 2032 notes and the USD 1,094.5 million term loan are 97.11% of principal and fall due in 2032 or 2033, with the term loan due in 2032 if the notes are not repaid, refinanced or extended, and the revolver matures in 2031. Apart from scheduled amortisation and a small amount of other debt, nothing falls due before 2031, so the credit case rests on refinancing the 2032 notes ahead of mid-2032.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22, 45–47; calculation C40; calculation C26

- The adjusted measure flatters the picture. Adjusted EBITDA exceeds reported EBITDA by 13.81% in FY2026, the largest add-back is share-based compensation, and USD 14.4 million of tariff refunds recognised in the last two quarters stays inside the measure; without it, net leverage on adjusted EBITDA would be 3.50x rather than 3.39x.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 55, 57, 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 35, 49; calculation C41; calculation C42

- Reported growth overstates underlying growth, and margins are lower. Revenue grew 9.80% in FY2026 and 8.20% in the September 2026 quarter, but organic constant-currency growth was 4% and 2%, with currency and acquisitions supplying the rest, while the adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 14.24% in FY2024 to 12.27% in FY2026 and 11.81% on a trailing basis, so growth is not yet converting into earnings.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest support is the June 2026 refinancing, which extended the term loan to 2033 and the revolver to 2031 and leaves no large maturity before 2031, together with steady cash interest cover and a seasonal pattern in which the December quarter carries the highest earnings: adjusted EBITDA in the December 2025 quarter was 1.41x the September 2025 quarter. A completed sale-leaseback of the Saxoprint facility, now held for sale, would cut net debt, and net leverage returning towards the 3.38x seen at June 2026 would reverse the concern. Further revolver drawings above USD 50.0 million, or a fall in trailing EBITDA, would strengthen it.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmpr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 49; calculation C45; calculation C37
### Limitations
- The fourth quarter of FY2026 is not reported in any readable source and is derived as the full year less nine months; the earnings release for that quarter holds no text.
- No balance sheet is supplied for June 2024 or September 2025, so leverage before June 2025 and a year-ago comparison of the latest quarter are not established.
- The term loan amortisation schedule is not stated, so the maturity ladder shows amortisation after the first year at final maturity and understates near-term repayments.
- The lender definition of EBITDA and the reported covenant ratio are not printed, so covenant headroom is not established, and the test definition changed on 4 June 2026.
- Reported EBITDA is calculated because the company prints only adjusted EBITDA, and the amount of letters of credit under the revolver is not stated separately.

spans.text: # CIMPRESS plc business and governance
## Request

Business and governance review of CIMPRESS plc (issuer id cmpr), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the consolidated Cimpress group: who owns and controls it, how its businesses earn money, and what its transactions and capital allocation mean for creditors. No transaction was specified for the run, so the transactions covered are those the filings report.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-08-07 | 151f9f0c267c42ae21f0ccdb2698ae7b00f08c12c11ea93c9eead2d225985251 | Business description, segments, ownership concentration, share repurchases, related-party note, noncontrolling interests, share-based awards, debt note, audit opinion, exhibits and subsequent events. |

| EX-99.1_2026-07-29_q4_fy26quarterlyearnings.htm.jsonl | Exhibit 99.1 earnings release for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 (file text holds the title line only) | not stated | b8846b3859a01d99986aba6cc0cb5d6c8ccc873cb9cf041c588ae8b2cd1b1c63 | Inspected for content; none usable, so no evidence was drawn from it. |

## Findings
### Bottom line

Business and governance risk for creditors is medium: Cimpress is a publicly owned, decentralised print group with no sponsor, whose stated priority is value per share rather than debt reduction, and whose earnings lean heavily on VistaPrint.

That priority has produced recurring share repurchases, which took 30.55% of operating cash flow over FY2024 to FY2026, and in 2026 a fresh USD 200 million authorisation and a EUR 120 million acquisition paid from cash and revolver borrowings. Beyond the Board's own discretion, only the debt documents, which were not supplied, limit how much cash can leave. VistaPrint earned 61.14% of segment EBITDA in FY2026, and growing minority put rights add a further call on cash.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 89–90; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 135–136; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; calculation A08; calculation A27
### Key findings

- No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, so creditors face public-market owners rather than a financial sponsor, but ownership is concentrated. About 70% of the ordinary shares are held by the top ten holders and only six holders sit on the register, while the beneficial ownership table lives in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so who the holders are and whether any of them controls the company is not established.

- Financial policy puts value per share ahead of debt reduction, which is the central governance risk for creditors. Management defines its uppermost objective as intrinsic value per share, in which net debt is a deduction, and says it accepts choices that look non-optimal on earnings or cash flow; the Board ties repurchases to net leverage and capital allocation priorities but may suspend them at any time, so the restraint is discretionary rather than contractual.

- Share repurchases have been the main shareholder payout; they have shrunk and have been paused since February 2026, but the capacity has been renewed. They took 44.76%, 26.09% and 17.65% of operating cash flow in FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026, 30.55% over the three years, and treasury shares stand at USD 1,363.55 million of cost against a shareholders' deficit. In March 2026 the Board replaced an authorisation with USD 65.2 million left by a fresh one of USD 200 million, so capacity to return cash is restored whenever the Board chooses.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 89–90; 10-Q_2026-03-31_cmpr-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; calculation A24; calculation A25; calculation A26; calculation A27; calculation A34

- Acquisition appetite is rising and is funded from cash and the revolver, with a sale-leaseback as the intended offset. Cash spent on acquisitions rose from 0.22% of operating cash flow in FY2025 to 11.42% in FY2026, and the purchase of Saxoprint and viaprinto on 2 July 2026, EUR 120 million subject to adjustment, took cash equal to 46.37% of FY2026 operating cash flow in a single quarter, using cash and USD 35.0 million drawn on the revolving credit facility; a manufacturing facility valued at 32.92% of the purchase consideration is held for sale, and no sale-leaseback agreement or proceeds are stated, so until one closes the purchase is a net call on group cash.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation A37; calculation A48; calculation A49; calculation A50

- Minority interests in subsidiaries are a growing claim on group cash that sits outside the debt. - Reporting is strong where the filings reach and thin where creditor protections sit. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern is restraint. Cimpress has never paid a dividend and does not expect to, repurchases fell from 44.76% to 17.65% of operating cash flow between FY2024 and FY2026 and have not been made since February 2026, the credit agreement restricts both dividends and purchases of ordinary shares, and the auditor and management report clean controls. A completed sale-leaseback of the Saxoprint facility, valued at 32.92% of the purchase consideration, would offset part of the acquisition cash. The view would improve if the executed documents showed tight limits on restricted payments, if the Board paired its repurchase authorisation with a debt reduction target, or if the sale-leaseback closed. It would worsen if repurchases resumed while the revolver stayed drawn, if the proxy statement showed one holder with control or board nominee rights, if the documents allowed wide capacity for shareholder payments, or if minority put payments exceeded their carrying value.

### Limitations

- The 2026 proxy statement was not supplied, so no holder is named and board independence, committee membership and nominee rights rest on the annual report alone; if one holder were shown to control the company, the finding that no one controls it would reverse.

- The executed credit agreement and 2032 notes indenture were not supplied, so the cash that may leave through repurchases, dividends and investments is not measured, and the finding that the debt documents constrain leakage rests on the company's own summary of them.

- The three earnings releases held no text, so management commentary on the timing of the Saxoprint sale-leaseback, on capital return intentions and on the Canva partnership is not available; the finding that repurchases are paused rests on the filings alone.
- Segment results before FY2026 are shown on an adjusted basis and the original figures are not supplied, so the easing of VistaPrint's share of earnings could differ on the earlier basis.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No single transaction defines this case, so the summary follows the filings. The largest recent transaction is the purchase of the Saxoprint and viaprinto businesses of CEWE Stiftung & Co. KGaA, completed on 2 July 2026 for EUR 120 million subject to a post-closing adjustment; the later quarterly report records a slightly higher euro consideration after adjustment, funded from cash and USD 35.0 million drawn on the revolving credit facility. The businesses sit in PrintBrothers, and the company approved a plan to sell and lease back the Saxoprint manufacturing facility, which is held for sale, but no agreement or proceeds are stated.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation A37

The only new debt issue in the period is the June 2026 amendment of the senior secured credit agreement, which extended the term loan to June 2033 and the revolver to June 2031, issued the term loan at 99.75% of par, and enlarged it to cover fees and add liquidity, with no other material change to terms. The earlier new issue, the USD 525 million 2032 senior unsecured notes, was placed under an indenture dated 26 September 2024 and funded the redemption of the senior notes due 2026.

Other transactions touch creditors indirectly. In the January to March 2026 quarter management teams bought 8.75% of each PrintBrothers business for EUR 21 million, creating a put right from 2036. In April 2026 Cimpress took a 50% interest with majority voting rights in one business for USD 20.0 million of cash and an 85% interest in another, and the Board replaced its share repurchase authorisation with a fresh USD 200 million one. No share was repurchased in the September 2026 quarter.

spans.text: # CIMPRESS plc fundamental credit
## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for CIMPRESS plc (issuer id cmpr), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the consolidated Cimpress group in US dollars: business quality, financial profile, liquidity, refinancing and downside, built on the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance work. No rating, relative value, recovery or legal conclusion is drawn.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Fundamental credit quality is adequate but weakening: a scaled, cash-generative print group with no large maturity before 2031 is carrying rising leverage, thinner liquidity and falling cash conversion into its seasonal peak, so creditors hold less cushion than a year ago.

Net debt stood at 3.93x trailing reported EBITDA at 30 September 2026, or 3.96x pro forma for a minority put payment due in the December 2026 quarter, against 3.38x at 30 June 2026, which precedes the July 2026 Saxoprint purchase and has no pro forma figure established. Adjusted free cash flow was 26.70% of adjusted EBITDA in FY2026 against 55.70% in FY2024, and cash plus undrawn revolver capacity fell to 0.19x of debt. The main downside path runs through VistaPrint, which earns 61.14% of segment EBITDA.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D03; calculation D04; calculation D02; calculation D12; calculation D10; calculation D21
### Key findings

- The refinancing runway is the main support, and the credit case rests on refinancing the 2032 notes before mid-2032. The notes and the term loan are 97.11% of principal; the term loan is due in June 2033 but moves to 16 June 2032 if the notes are not repaid, refinanced or extended, and the revolver matures in 2031 with 14.0% drawn. Nothing material falls due before 2031 apart from scheduled amortisation and small other debt, so near-term repayment is not the pressure point.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; calculation D19; calculation D11

- Leverage has stepped up and the cushion is thinner. Net debt rose 11.80% in the September 2026 quarter because Saxoprint was paid for from cash and the revolver while trailing EBITDA slipped, taking net leverage on reported EBITDA from 3.38x at June to 3.93x, or 3.96x pro forma for the minority put payment due in the December 2026 quarter. On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the ratio is 3.39x, and 3.50x without the tariff refunds that sit in the adjusted figure. No pro forma for the July 2026 purchase is established against the June figure.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D01; calculation D02; calculation D03; calculation D04; calculation D05; calculation D06; calculation D07

- Liquidity is at its seasonal low and has thinned sharply. Cash fell 51.73% in the quarter and undrawn revolver capacity fell from USD 232.7 million to USD 197.7 million, so cash plus undrawn capacity is 0.19x of total debt against 0.30x at June. The leverage covenant applies only when drawings exceed 20% of commitments, which is USD 50.0 million against USD 35.0 million drawn, so USD 15.0 million more would put the test into play; the lender-defined ratio is not printed.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation D08; calculation D09; calculation D10; calculation D11

- Cash conversion is the weakest dimension and is still falling. Adjusted free cash flow was 55.70%, 34.17% and 26.70% of adjusted EBITDA in FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026, while capital spending including software rose from 3.44% to 4.48% of revenue; EBITDA less that spending covered cash interest only 2.05x on a trailing basis. Less internally generated cash is left for debt reduction at a time when buybacks, acquisitions and minority puts compete for it.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D12; calculation D13; calculation D14

- Margins are eroding faster than growth is converting into earnings. Revenue grew 9.80% in FY2026 but organic constant-currency growth was 4%, while cost of revenue rose from 51.5% to 53.7% of revenue and the adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 14.24% in FY2024 to 12.27% in FY2026 and 11.81% on a trailing basis. Start-up costs for the North American network, tariffs, duties and energy explain most of the latest quarter's decline, so margin recovery depends on that investment paying back.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 58–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D15; calculation D16; calculation D22

- VistaPrint is both the main strength and the single point of failure. It earned 61.14% of segment EBITDA in FY2026 at a segment margin of 20.29%, down from 63.60% a year earlier, and its segment EBITDA fell 10% in the September 2026 quarter, with its share at 60.26%, on start-up costs, Canadian duties and advertising while legacy products declined 2%. Group earnings therefore still rest on small-business demand and on one network investment.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation D21

- Financial policy is the swing factor and sits outside the debt. Share repurchases took 30.55% of operating cash flow over FY2024 to FY2026, the Board renewed a USD 200 million authorisation in March 2026, and redeemable minority interests are 4.11x their June 2025 level, so cash can leave the group through channels that do not reduce leverage.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D23; calculation D24

- Interest cover is steady but rate-exposed. EBITDA covered cash interest 3.34x, 3.67x and 3.54x at June 2025, June 2026 and September 2026, and 4.11x on the adjusted measure, yet 67.73% of principal floats on Term SOFR and a 100 bp rise would add USD 7.4 million to annual interest after swaps, so cover is protected mainly by earnings holding up.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D17; calculation D18

- Tariffs are a live but bounded cost. The primary effect is on promotional products sourced from China and other countries, broad tariffs of 10% to 12.5% replaced an expired global rate on 24 July 2026, and a 50% tariff on certain Canadian goods followed in August, while USD 14.4 million of refunds already sit in adjusted EBITDA and about USD 10 million of further claims are not recognised.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D20
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a weakening view is the structure of the debt and the seasonal rebuild. No large maturity falls due before 2031, interest cover has held between 3.34x and 3.67x, and cash rose 28.69% between September and December 2025 as the December quarter delivered adjusted EBITDA of 1.41x the September quarter, so the September 2026 trough may reverse. Management also has levers: repurchases have been paused since February 2026, capital spending is 4.48% of revenue, and a completed sale-leaseback of the Saxoprint facility, valued at 32.92% of the purchase consideration, would cut net debt. The view would improve if net leverage returned towards 3.38x after the December 2026 quarter and cash conversion stopped falling. It would worsen if drawings passed USD 50.0 million, if trailing EBITDA kept falling, or if repurchases resumed while the revolver stayed drawn.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D02; calculation D11; calculation D13; calculation D17; calculation D25
### Limitations

- No ratings, market prices, peer figures or company guidance were supplied, so refinancing capacity rests on maturity timing and reported results alone; if market access proved impaired, the finding that the 2032 maturity is manageable would weaken.
- The December cash rebuild is observed once, in the 2025 quarter, because earlier balance sheets are absent; if the December 2026 quarter is weaker, the contrary case for liquidity would fail.
- The springing leverage test cannot be measured against any covenant ratio, so the downside scenario treats drawings above USD 50.0 million as a warning signal rather than a breach point.
- No sector or peer data were supplied, so the judgement that the business profile is adequate rests on the issuer's own record and not on a comparison with other leveraged issuers.
### Strengths and weaknesses
The main credit strengths are these.

- Scale and VistaPrint economics anchor earnings. VistaPrint serves millions of small businesses a year at a segment margin of 20.29% and about 55% gross margin, collects from customers before production and needs little inventory, so it funds the group's cash generation and supports debt service even when other segments earn less.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 135–136; calculation D21
- The maturity profile gives time. Nearly all principal is due in 2032 and 2033, with the revolver in 2031, so the first test is a refinancing window rather than repayment.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D19
- Interest cover is steady. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest 3.54x on a trailing basis and the adjusted measure 4.11x, so a modest earnings dip does not immediately threaten debt service.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D17

- Operating flexibility exists. Capital spending of 4.48% of revenue goes mostly to equipment and network expansion that management chooses to undertake, although the split between maintenance and growth is not stated, repurchases are paused and the December quarter carries the peak earnings, which gives management room to rebuild cash.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 69; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D13; calculation D25

- Reporting quality supports monitoring. The auditor gave an unqualified opinion and controls are reported effective, so the financial figures can be relied on even where creditor terms are not visible.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)
The main credit weaknesses are these.

- Leverage is high and rising. Net debt of 3.93x trailing reported EBITDA, or 3.96x pro forma for the minority put payment due in the December 2026 quarter, leaves little room before the 2032 refinancing if earnings keep slipping.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D03; calculation D04

- Cash conversion is falling. Adjusted free cash flow fell to 26.70% of adjusted EBITDA in FY2026 from 55.70% in FY2024 as capital spending and cost of revenue rose, which reduces the cash available to repay debt.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D12; calculation D16
- Margins are compressing. The adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 11.81% on a trailing basis from 14.24% in FY2024, and tariffs, duties, energy and start-up costs are still in the run rate.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation D15
- Earnings are concentrated. VistaPrint produced 61.14% of segment EBITDA, so a shock to small-business demand or to North American cross-border costs reaches most of the cash flow.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D21
- Financial policy competes with debt reduction. Repurchases, acquisitions and minority puts draw on the same cash, and the debt documents that would limit them were not supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D23; calculation D24

### Company description

Cimpress is a web-to-print group that sells customised marketing print, signage, packaging, promotional products, apparel and design services, mainly to small businesses and graphic professionals, through five autonomous segments. Revenue was USD 3.7 billion in FY2026, split 51.55% VistaPrint, 21.65% PrintBrothers, 10.48% The Print Group, 10.74% National Pen and 5.58% All Other Businesses, with 50.11% earned in Europe and 45.91% in North America. The model gives revenue visibility only at the order level: small orders, paid up front at VistaPrint, repeat purchase and a December peak, so cash generation is supported by prepayment and low inventory but not by contracts.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 135
### Ownership and group structure

No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed; about 70% of the shares sit with the top ten holders and the board and nominee detail is not supplied. The borrowers are Cimpress plc and five named subsidiaries, certain subsidiaries guarantee both the secured facility and the notes, and the guarantor names are not supplied. Financial policy is therefore set by a public board that defines value per share as its objective, and creditor protection rests on documents that were not provided.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is discretionary and small-business driven, with limited pricing power: the annual report says customers are price-sensitive and past pricing changes moved order volumes, and free social media channels are a substitute when small firms cut spending. Organic constant-currency growth was 4% in FY2026 and 2% in the September 2026 quarter, with currency and acquisitions supplying the rest of the reported 9.80%, and growth is led by elevated products while certain legacy products fell 2%. Revenue is therefore moderately durable but cyclical, and the credit consequence is that earnings can fall quickly in a small-business downturn while debt service is fixed.
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins can be defended only partly. Cost of revenue rose from 51.5% to 53.7% of revenue over FY2024 to FY2026 on higher fulfilment, manufacturing and shipping costs, while marketing and selling spend fell from 24.0% to 23.3% of revenue, so gross profit pressure outweighed operating leverage. The cost base is largely variable through third-party fulfilment and advertising, but production assets, platform costs and cloud commitments are fixed; the credit consequence is that volume shortfalls hit margins before costs adjust.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 141; calculation D16
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is moderate but rising and is the main drag on conversion. Capital spending including capitalised software was 4.48% of revenue in FY2026, mostly manufacturing and automation equipment and the North American network, and adjusted free cash flow was only 26.70% of adjusted EBITDA. Working capital is seasonal, with inventory built in the September quarter and released into the December peak, and a supplier finance programme sits inside payables. Cash conversion is therefore adequate in a good year and weak in a year of heavy investment, and the credit consequence is slower deleveraging.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 140; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D12; calculation D13
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense in a fragmented market, which limits pricing, while scale and central purchasing give Cimpress a cost edge over smaller printers. The threat of substitutes is rising through free social media channels and artificial intelligence products that compete in design services and content creation. Buyer power is high because small customers are price-sensitive and switch easily, and supplier power is moderate because paper, ink and equipment are bought centrally and hundreds of external fulfillers supply capacity. The credit consequence is that margins have little pricing buffer, so cost shocks pass into earnings.
### Macro, policy and technology factors

Trade policy is the policy factor that matters to credit. The annual report describes volatile United States tariffs, with broad tariffs of 10% to 12.5% from 24 July 2026 and a 50% tariff on certain Canadian goods from August 2026, mainly affecting promotional products and goods fulfilled from Canada for United States customers, and the refund of invalidated duties has so far added USD 14.4 million to adjusted EBITDA. Currency lifted FY2026 revenue growth by 4%, so a weaker euro or sterling would reduce reported earnings, and new European forestry and sustainability rules add compliance cost from December 2026. Credit consequence: tariff and currency swings move EBITDA by tens of millions of dollars, against interest cover of 3.54x.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 57–59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D17; calculation D20
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are the VistaPrint franchise, the 2031 to 2033 maturity profile and prepayment-funded cash generation; weaknesses are falling cash conversion, margin compression and high leverage. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are elevated products, the Canva partnership and a Saxoprint sale-leaseback; threats are tariffs and duties, artificial intelligence substitution, a small-business downturn and a financial policy that favours distributions or deals over debt reduction.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 57; calculation D03
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position is strong on evidence: the group says it is the largest in its space, with USD 3.7 billion of revenue and VistaPrint at a 20.29% segment margin. Competitive advantage is average, resting on scale purchasing and the platform but with price-sensitive buyers. Business diversification is average, because VistaPrint produces 61.14% of segment EBITDA even though five segments and two continents are present. Cost and capex flexibility is average, margin stability is weak, and free cash flow stability is weak, given conversion of 26.70% and a margin down 2.43 percentage points since FY2024. The ability to refinance is average, on a long runway but no market evidence. Liquidity is weak at the seasonal low, at 0.19x of debt, and financial policy and governance is average, with transparent reporting but a value-per-share objective that competes with debt reduction. The trend is weakening.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D10; calculation D12; calculation D15; calculation D21; calculation D26
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 months to 24 months the December 2026 quarter decides whether cash and leverage recover: it carries the peak earnings, and the Saxoprint integration, the planned sale-leaseback and a further claim of about USD 10 million for tariff refunds are tailwinds, against headwinds from start-up costs for the North American network, tariffs, energy and a minority put payment. Over three years to five years the question is whether elevated products and the platform lift margins before the 2032 refinancing, and whether financial policy favours debt reduction when the notes approach their window. There is no company guidance in the sources, so the outlook is an analytical reading.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_cmpr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D25
### Downside scenario

The most credible downside begins with weaker small-business demand or higher cross-border tariffs while North American start-up costs persist. VistaPrint, which earns 61.14% of segment EBITDA, loses volume and margin first; group EBITDA falls, and adjusted free cash flow, already 26.70% of adjusted EBITDA, turns negative after capital spending. A 10% fall in trailing reported EBITDA, with net debt unchanged, would lift net leverage to 4.37x, or 4.40x pro forma for the minority put payment due in the December 2026 quarter. Cash and USD 197.7 million of undrawn capacity cover the seasonal trough, but drawings above USD 50.0 million bring the leverage test into play, and the next levers are to stop repurchases, slow capital spending and complete the sale-leaseback. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through the December quarter, but the margin for a second weak year is thin.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cmpr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation D11; calculation D12; calculation D21; calculation D26
### Overall credit view

Overall, Cimpress presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, a prepaid VistaPrint franchise and a runway to 2032, but credit quality is constrained by rising leverage, falling cash conversion and margin compression. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but weakening because capital spending and cost of revenue are rising faster than earnings. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA recovering before the notes approach their June 2032 window, and on the financial policy staying restrained. The primary downside path is a VistaPrint earnings shortfall that turns free cash flow negative while leverage is already high. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, ratings and market evidence, and management guidance. Top risk: VistaPrint earnings concentration combined with thin liquidity at the seasonal low.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D03; calculation D12; calculation D21
